requirements.requirement: Configure opsadmin on node1 for SSH access with the specified ed25519 public key installed in authorized_keys
requirements.summary: Baseline showed opsadmin did not exist (cmd-bdebc510151c40f0). Executor created the user, set up .ssh directory with correct permissions, and installed exactly the required public key into authorized_keys with proper ownership (700/600) (cmd-fee234018dc34f57, cmd-bc4cc5c41547444f). Post-reboot state confirms the user and exact key persisted (cmd-6f4a456e7f334016).

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication (disable password/keyboard-interactive authentication)
requirements.summary: Baseline sshd_config had commented-out (default/ambiguous) auth directives (cmd-bdebc510151c40f0). Executor wrote /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf setting PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes, validated syntax with sshd -t and effective config with sshd -T, and reloaded sshd (cmd-2e90ada5ba9f495d, cmd-d4432d61598b471b, cmd-7042d748d8784f24). Functional verification with a real SSH client showed pubkey login succeeding and password login being rejected outright with no interactive prompt, both before and after the reboot (cmd-adc33a7f6ac64c24, cmd-109d0304a3fc4bf0).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol demonstrating healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered state on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 8c28f3cd..., uptime, active sshd, key-only settings, and opsadmin/authorized_keys state (cmd-2b08219bdd544256), matching the fixed before-prepare boot-identity observation. Reboot was acknowledged and the node was confirmed down mid-transition (cmd-dadb749d16a74cd5, cmd-3e7f6c372d3a4ba9), then exec access was confirmed restored (cmd-adc9dcecc4b848b0). Post-restart capture shows a different boot_id (d3c1ba32...) matching the fixed after-executor snapshot, with sshd active, key-only config intact, and opsadmin/authorized_keys/locked-shadow entry recovered (cmd-6f4a456e7f334016). A final live SSH functional test after reboot confirmed pubkey login success and password login rejection (cmd-109d0304a3fc4bf0).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating opsadmin with the specified public key and enforcing key-based-only SSH authentication — are satisfied with direct functional evidence (successful pubkey login, outright-rejected password login) captured both before and after a full node reboot. The independent restart-evidence protocol is also well-documented: healthy pre-restart baseline, acknowledged restart with confirmed disconnection, a changed boot identity matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and fully recovered service/user/config state post-restart.
limitations: The password-authentication rejection test relies on the executor's own SSH client output rather than an independently reproduced login attempt, though the transcript (Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic)) is consistent with password auth being disabled.
No independent verification of file permissions/ownership beyond what the executor's own stat/cat commands report.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 18 executor commands chronologically. Password-lock of opsadmin (cmd-c24ad8fb2d544ea9, verified cmd-572c3e530ee14804) is a reasonable, low-risk hardening step directly supporting the 'require key-based SSH authentication' outcome, not an unnecessary mutation. Two temporary SSH test keypairs were added to authorized_keys to functionally validate auth behavior (cmd-adc33a7f6ac64c24 pre-reboot, cmd-109d0304a3fc4bf0 post-reboot) and both were fully removed/restored immediately afterward, leaving authorized_keys containing only the required key (cmd-5fff3cc57c9e4e22, and the restore step within cmd-109d0304a3fc4bf0). These were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted, directly tied to collecting final evidence for the auth requirement. No abandoned files, failed/conflicting services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were observed; failed-services and package-health snapshots are clean before and after (global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:package-health). Sshd listening sockets and PID changed only due to the required reboot, not an unrelated action.
